title: A Multi-Labeled Dataset for Indonesian Discourse: Examining Toxicity, Polarization, and Demographics Information

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the gap in inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) on toxicity and polarization between annotators with different presidential vote leanings, and evaluating model performance when conditioned on annotator political preferences.

Measuring the gap in inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) on toxicity and polarization between disabled and non-disabled annotators, and evaluating model performance when conditioned on annotator disability status.

Measuring the gap in inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) on toxicity and polarization among annotators from different geographic domiciles (e.g., Greater Jakarta vs. Non-Java), and evaluating model performance when conditioned on annotator domicile.

Measuring the gap in inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) on toxicity and polarization among annotators from different age groups/generations (e.g., Gen X, Millennials, Gen Z), and evaluating model performance when conditioned on annotator age.

Measuring the gap in inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) on toxicity and polarization between annotators of different ethnic backgrounds (e.g., Indigenous vs. Non-Indigenous), and evaluating model performance when conditioned on annotator ethnicity.

Measuring the gap in inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) on toxicity and polarization between annotators of different religious beliefs (e.g., Islam vs. Non-Islam), and evaluating model performance when conditioned on annotator religion.
Measuring the gap in inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) on toxicity and polarization between male and female annotators, and evaluating model performance when conditioned on annotator gender.

Measuring the gap in inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) on toxicity and polarization among annotators with different education levels, and evaluating model performance when conditioned on annotator education.

Measuring the gap in inter-annotator agreement (Gwet's AC1) on toxicity and polarization among annotators with different employment statuses (e.g., Employed, Unemployed, Student), and evaluating model performance when conditioned on annotator job status.
